IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: IEEE 802.11e-2005 or 802.11e is an approved amendment to the IEEE 802.11 standard that defines a set of quality of service (QoS) enhancements for wireless LAN applications through modifications to the media access control (MAC) layer.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: This is available only in "infrastructure" mode, where stations are connected to the network through an _____ (AP)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: This is available only in "infrastructure" mode, where stations are connected to the network through an Access Point (AP).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: APs send beacon frames at regular intervals (usually every 100 TU or 0._____ second)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: APs send beacon frames at regular intervals (usually every 100 TU or 0.1024 second).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Between these beacon frames, PCF defines two periods: the _____ (CFP) and the Contention Period (CP)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Between these beacon frames, PCF defines two periods: the Contention Free Period (CFP) and the Contention Period (CP).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: In the CFP, the AP sends _____-Free-Poll (CF-Poll) packets to each station, one at a time, to give them the right to send a packet
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Between these beacon frames, PCF defines two periods: the Contention Free Period (CFP) and the Contention Period (CP). In the CFP, the AP sends Contention-Free-Poll (CF-Poll) packets to each station, one at a time, to give them the right to send a packet.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Within the HCF, there are two methods of channel accessed, similar to those defined in the legacy 802.11 MAC: HCF _____ (HCCA) and Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Within the HCF, there are two methods of channel accessed, similar to those defined in the legacy 802.11 MAC: HCF Controlled Channel Access (HCCA) and Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Both EDCA and HCCA define _____ (TC)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Both EDCA and HCCA define Traffic Categories (TC).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: This is accomplished through the _____ protocol, which is a variation of CSMA/CA using a shorter arbitration inter-frame space (AIFS) for higher priority packets
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: This is accomplished through the TCMA protocol, which is a variation of CSMA/CA using a shorter arbitration inter-frame space (AIFS) for higher priority packets.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: In addition, EDCA provides contention-free access to the channel for a period called a _____ (TXOP)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: In addition, EDCA provides contention-free access to the channel for a period called a Transmit Opportunity (TXOP).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: A _____ is a bounded time interval during which a station can send as many frames as possible (as long as the duration of the transmissions does not extend beyond the maximum duration of the TXOP)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: In addition, EDCA provides contention-free access to the channel for a period called a Transmit Opportunity (TXOP). A TXOP is a bounded time interval during which a station can send as many frames as possible (as long as the duration of the transmissions does not extend beyond the maximum duration of the TXOP).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: If a frame is too large to be transmitted in a single _____, it should be fragmented into smaller frames
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: In addition, EDCA provides contention-free access to the channel for a period called a Transmit Opportunity (TXOP). A TXOP is a bounded time interval during which a station can send as many frames as possible (as long as the duration of the transmissions does not extend beyond the maximum duration of the TXOP).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: The use of _____ reduces the problem of low rate stations gaining an inordinate amount of channel time in the legacy 802.11 DCF MAC
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: The use of TXOPs reduces the problem of low rate stations gaining an inordinate amount of channel time in the legacy 802.11 DCF MAC.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: A _____ time interval of 0 means it is limited to a single MAC service data unit (MSDU) or MAC management protocol data unit (MMPDU)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: A TXOP is a bounded time interval during which a station can send as many frames as possible (as long as the duration of the transmissions does not extend beyond the maximum duration of the TXOP). If a frame is too large to be transmitted in a single TXOP, it should be fragmented into smaller frames.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: The levels of priority in _____ are called access categories (ACs)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: The levels of priority in EDCA are called access categories (ACs).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: The C_____ and CWmax values are calculated from aCWmin and aCWmax values, respectively, that are defined for each physical layer supported by 802.11e
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: The CWmin and CWmax values are calculated from aCWmin and aCWmax values, respectively, that are defined for each physical layer supported by 802.11e. For a typical of aCWmin=15 and aCWmax=1023, as used, for example, by OFDM (802.11a) and MIMO (802.11n), the resulting values are as following: ACs map directly from Ethernet-level class of service (CoS) priority levels: The primary purpose of QoS is to protect high priority data from low priority data.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Wi-_____ (WMM) is the Wi-Fi Alliance specification which is a subset of IEEE 802.11e
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Wi-Fi Multimedia (WMM) is the Wi-Fi Alliance specification which is a subset of IEEE 802.11e.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Certified APs must be enabled for _____ and TXOP
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Certified APs must be enabled for EDCA and TXOP.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: However, in contrast to PCF, in which the interval between two beacon frames is divided into two periods of CFP and CP, the _____ allows for CFPs being initiated at almost anytime during a CP
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: However, in contrast to PCF, in which the interval between two beacon frames is divided into two periods of CFP and CP, the HCCA allows for CFPs being initiated at almost anytime during a CP.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: This kind of CFP is called a _____ (CAP) in 802.11e
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: This kind of CFP is called a Controlled Access Phase (CAP) in 802.11e.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: During a CAP, the _____ (HC)—which is also the AP—controls the access to the medium
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: During a CAP, the Hybrid Coordinator (HC)—which is also the AP—controls the access to the medium.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: During the CP, all stations function in _____
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: During the CP, all stations function in EDCA.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: The other difference with the PCF is that _____ (TC) and Traffic Streams (TS) are defined
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: The other difference with the PCF is that Traffic Class (TC) and Traffic Streams (TS) are defined. Moreover, the stations give info about the lengths of their queues for each Traffic Class (TC).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Moreover, the stations give info about the lengths of their queues for each _____ (TC)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: The other difference with the PCF is that Traffic Class (TC) and Traffic Streams (TS) are defined. Moreover, the stations give info about the lengths of their queues for each Traffic Class (TC).

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Another difference is that stations are given a _____: they may send multiple packets in a row, for a given time period selected by the HC
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Another difference is that stations are given a TXOP: they may send multiple packets in a row, for a given time period selected by the HC.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: During the CFP, the HC allows stations to send data by sending CF-_____ frames
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: During the CFP, the HC allows stations to send data by sending CF-Poll frames.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: With the _____, QoS can be configured with great precision
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: HCCA is generally considered the most advanced (and complex) coordination function. With the HCCA, QoS can be configured with great precision.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: In fact, few (if any) APs currently available are enabled for _____
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With the HCCA, QoS can be configured with great precision. HCCA support is not mandatory for 802.11e APs.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Implementing the _____ on end stations uses the existing DCF mechanism for channel access (no change to DCF or EDCA operation is needed)
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: HCCA support is not mandatory for 802.11e APs. In fact, few (if any) APs currently available are enabled for HCCA.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: With _____, multiple frames may be transmitted together by the access point to a power-saving device during a service period
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: APSD (automatic power save delivery) provides two ways to start delivery: ‘scheduled APSD’ (S-APSD) and ‘unscheduled APSD’ (U-APSD). With APSD, multiple frames may be transmitted together by the access point to a power-saving device during a service period.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: With S-APSD, service periods start according to a predetermined schedule known to the power-saving device, thus allowing the _____ to transmit its buffered traffic without the need for any signaling
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With APSD, multiple frames may be transmitted together by the access point to a power-saving device during a service period. With S-APSD, service periods start according to a predetermined schedule known to the power-saving device, thus allowing the Access Point to transmit its buffered traffic without the need for any signaling.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: With U-APSD, whenever a frame is sent to the _____, a service period is triggered, which allows the access point to send buffered frames in the other direction
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With APSD, multiple frames may be transmitted together by the access point to a power-saving device during a service period. With S-APSD, service periods start according to a predetermined schedule known to the power-saving device, thus allowing the Access Point to transmit its buffered traffic without the need for any signaling.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: U-_____ can take a ‘full’ U-APSD or ‘hybrid’ U-APSD form
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With S-APSD, service periods start according to a predetermined schedule known to the power-saving device, thus allowing the Access Point to transmit its buffered traffic without the need for any signaling. With U-APSD, whenever a frame is sent to the Access Point, a service period is triggered, which allows the access point to send buffered frames in the other direction.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: With Hybrid U-APSD, either U-APSD or the legacy _____ mechanism is used, depending on the access category
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With Hybrid U-APSD, either U-APSD or the legacy Power Save Polling mechanism is used, depending on the access category. APSD is a more efficient power management method than legacy 802.11 Power Save Polling, leading to lower power consumption, as it reduces both the signaling traffic that would otherwise be needed for delivery of buffered frames to power-saving devices by an AP and the collision rate among power-save polls, typically transmitted immediately after the beacon TIM.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: S-_____ is available for both channel access mechanisms, EDCA and HCCA, while U-APSD is available only for EDCA
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: With U-APSD, whenever a frame is sent to the Access Point, a service period is triggered, which allows the access point to send buffered frames in the other direction. U-APSD can take a ‘full’ U-APSD or ‘hybrid’ U-APSD form.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Hybrid U-APSD is less efficient than Full U-APSD because the _____ mechanism it employs for some access categories is less efficient than APSD, as explained above
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Hybrid U-APSD is less efficient than Full U-APSD because the Power Save Polling mechanism it employs for some access categories is less efficient than APSD, as explained above.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Frames with _____ are not acknowledged
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Frames with QosNoAck are not acknowledged.

IEEE 802.11e-2005.subject: Meteorology & Climate
IEEE 802.11e-2005.question: Tunnelled Direct Link Setup was published as 802.11z (_____), allowing devices to perform more efficient direct station-to-station frame transfers without support from the AP
IEEE 802.11e-2005.fact: Tunnelled Direct Link Setup was published as 802.11z (TDLS), allowing devices to perform more efficient direct station-to-station frame transfers without support from the AP. Both DLS and TDLS require that stations be associated with the same AP.
